name: only a 503 is retried again
why: The original org/503-handling.org F6 defect, reverted verbatim. Every widened status must notice; 502 is the representative here and 429/504 have their own entries below.

name: 429 dropped from the transient set
why: Only the 429 test may notice. If 502/504 fail too, the set is being read somewhere it should not be.

name: 502 dropped from the transient set
why: Attribution: a single missing member must be traceable to the status it belongs to, which is why these are one test per status rather than one loop.

name: 504 dropped from the transient set
why: As above. 504 is the one a reverse proxy returns on a slow upstream, i.e. the most likely to be met in practice and the least likely to be noticed if dropped.

name: the set is bypassed — every 4xx/5xx retried
why: The overshoot, not the defect: widening a retry set is exactly the change that goes too far. Without the boundary test a set that swallowed 400/403/500 would look identical to a correct one, and every failure on the page would cost three attempts instead of one.

name: Retry-After is never read
why: The header half of F6. 503 was already retried, so only the WAIT changes: the retry lands at the bare backoff (~1100 ms) instead of the 3000 ms the server asked for.

name: the hint is not passed to beforeRetry
why: Drops the second argument at the one place it is handed over. Every caller then computes Math.max(delay, undefined) = NaN and setTimeout(fn, NaN) fires at once, so the per-caller backoff goes too — measured gap 1100 ms, which is _relAwaitRateSlot() alone still holding the line. Worth knowing: the rate gate MASKS a lost backoff, so a spec that only checked 'was there a pause' would not see this.

name: the 30 s cap is removed
why: A maintenance window answering `Retry-After: 3600` would park a request for an hour with nothing on screen explaining it. Only the __saTest assertion can see this — a behavioural test would have to wait out the cap.

name: delta-seconds parsed as an HTTP-date
why: Removes the numeric branch, so `Retry-After: 12` reaches Date.parse() — which succeeds on some engines as the year 12, i.e. a date two millennia in the past, silently discarded as 0. The likeliest way to break this parser while it still looks correct for the date form.

name: _relFetchWs2's beforeRetry ignores the hint
why: The floor is applied per call site, written out three times. This is the per-entity Relationships lookup — the one the click-to-load path uses.

name: _msFetchOneBatch's beforeRetry ignores the hint
why: The second call site. A shared classifier that only one consumer actually honours is the failure this covers.

edits.find:
beforeRetry: (attempt, retryAfterMs) => new Promise(
                r => setTimeout(r, Math.max(_MS_BATCH_DELAY * attempt, retryAfterMs))),
edits.replace:
beforeRetry: (attempt, retryAfterMs) => new Promise(
                r => setTimeout(r, _MS_BATCH_DELAY * attempt)),

grep: a 502 on a batch is retried

name: _relBrowseFetchPage's beforeRetry ignores the hint
why: The third call site, and the quietest: a failed browse page does not surface as an error at all — the loop just breaks and per-row lookups take over. The browse test counts the two request kinds apart for exactly that reason.
